set.tovw: Merchants fed him gold for years; house searched 1897, nothing found; hoard $1,000-3,000 if real

tw-mi-north-muskegon-chilson-gold.st: The Chronicle (16 Jun 1897) names merchants J. E. Balkema and Iver Anderson, who had a standing arrangement to swap him every gold piece they took in for paper; he lived on a $12 pension. North Muskegon opinion put the hoard at not less than $3,000, hidden or banked; his brother Richard said under $1,000. A diligent search of the house found no money, and the coroner had the house locked and guarded. No later find.

set.tovw: Deathbed tale, implausible sum ($308,000), no find

tw-mi-muskegon-larson-norwegian-coin.st: State-column versions (Feb 1903) name the digger James Anderson, the dead man Ole Larson and the sum '$308,000 in Norwegian coin', told on his deathbed to Adolph Miller.
